headline: High: Gemini CLI can write shared files and use MCP, while whisper is local-only and non-tooling, so prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are limited but real; no direct data-leak path is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use user-configured MCP servers, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs could be treated as instructions. whisper has no tool use or filesystem read/write, so it is not an active injector, but it can still be the source of transcribed text that Gemini CLI may parse. The interaction is plausible, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI ingests text from shared files or MCP outputs as instructions, injection is possible.
IF whisper-transcribed content is copied into Gemini CLI prompts or files, malicious text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not strictly needed.
Keep whisper outputs in a separate directory from Gemini CLI workspaces.
Require a human review step before Gemini CLI executes instructions from transcribed text.
Use a prompt template that labels imported text as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between transcription and agent prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while whisper only touches audio files and has no network egress or filesystem read/write. The pair does not show a shared workspace or shared OAuth principal, so a direct leakage path is not evidenced. Any leak would require manual transfer of sensitive content between the two.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies sensitive transcripts or code between the two tools, leakage can occur.
IF both are pointed at the same directory through external orchestration, shared-file exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep audio/transcript files outside the coding workspace.
Do not paste whisper output into Gemini CLI unless redacted.
Run Gemini CLI in a separate user account or container.
Delete temporary transcripts after use.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; whisper cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict is indirect if an external wrapper feeds whisper outputs into Gemini-managed files, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator writes whisper outputs into the same git tree Gemini CLI edits, file contention can occur.
IF Gemini CLI is run concurrently in multiple terminals against the same repo, git conflicts can arise.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo.
Use separate branches for Gemini CLI work.
Keep whisper outputs outside the git repository.
Commit frequently to reduce merge scope.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can act on files and shell commands, so if whisper output is treated as authoritative transcription or facts, downstream mistakes can cascade into incorrect edits or commands. whisper itself is not an action-taking agent, but its output can still be consumed without verification by Gemini CLI. The pathway exists in default human workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses whisper output as ground truth without human verification, transcription errors can propagate.
IF Gemini CLI converts transcript content into shell commands or code edits, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Verify transcripts before acting on them.
Require a second pass for any command or code generated from whisper output.
Limit Gemini CLI to drafting, not executing, when using transcripts.
Keep a changelog of transcript-to-action mappings.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before auto-actioning transcript-derived content.

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while whisper handles audio/speech and has no stated residency or retention mismatch. No PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data pathway is documented in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to operator handling rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated audio is transcribed and then stored in Gemini CLI workspaces, retention obligations may apply.
IF the operator routes EU PII or PHI through either tool outside approved controls, compliance issues can arise.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces.
Redact transcripts before using Gemini CLI.
Confirm retention settings for any storage location.
Use local-only handling for sensitive audio.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and retention controls for the workflow.
